text:
Cutter Gauthier has scored in nine straight games, 16 goals in all, and the Los Angeles Times notes it's the NHL's longest goal streak in 29 years. Through 20 games he has 18. The fun question is how much of it is real, and the answer is more than you'd think. He's on the ice for 88% of Anaheim's power-play chances, up from 55% last season, and his own chances have climbed to 1.64 expected goals per 60 minutes (shot quality, scaled to ice time) from 1.36. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking already had him in the 99th percentile for chances from in front of the net last season.

The rest is finishing. He's at 18 goals on 10.1 expected, shooting 21% against 14% last season, and Anaheim is getting outchanced at five on five with him out there (45.9% of expected goals). That rate rarely holds. The skill under it does: a 95 mph top shot, among the hardest in the league, and a role that now puts him on the ice for nearly every power play. Whatever happens to the streak, that role looks like his.
